title: A Warm Goodbye: How to Make Daycare Separation Easier for Our Child
summary:
The clock hands move towards daycare time, and your heart tightens a little as you imagine your little girl's (2-3 years old) tears as she clings to you. This scene repeats every morning, leaving you feeling guilty and confused. Is this normal? Is there anything that can be done to alleviate this anxiety that fills her small eyes at the classroom door?

Rest assured, this crying is not a sign of weakness or a mistake on your part; rather, it is a healthy sign of her secure attachment to you. Separation anxiety at this age is very normal and often peaks between 18 months and 3 years. Your child does not understand the concept of time as we do, so your absence may seem endless to her. Sneaking away without a goodbye, though it may seem easier for a moment, breaks her trust and makes every subsequent separation harder because it lacks the element of security and predictability.

The key lies in consistency and clarity. Create a short, consistent goodbye ritual: the same word, the same hug, the same kiss. Make it quick and decisive. Link your return to something tangible your child understands, such as "I'll be back after naptime" or "after lunch." The most important thing is to stick to this time. Do not go back into the classroom if they cry, and do not cancel your plans because of it. Your consistency in returning at the agreed-upon time builds a bridge of trust that gradually reduces their anxiety and gives them the security they need to know that you will always return.
try_this: Today: Create a consistent and very short goodbye ritual (one word and one hug), and repeat it exactly when dropping your child off at daycare or a club. Do not return to the classroom no matter how much they cry after the goodbye.
reflection_prompts: Is your goodbye ritual for your child consistent and brief, or does it vary each day and increase their confusion?
Do you stick to the agreed-upon return time with your child, even if the goodbye is difficult?
parent_script: “I love you, my little one. I’ll be back after naptime.”
assistant_prompts: How do I deal with my child's intense crying when leaving them at daycare for the first time?
What activities can help my child adjust to my absence at daycare?
